newsitem.title: FRANCE: France should be flexible on privatisation - Jospin.
newsitem.headline: France should be flexible on privatisation - Jospin.

text.p: Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said on Thursday that France should be flexible about privatising state enterprises and not turn its back on industrial reality for the sake of ideology.

In his first television interview since taking office a month ago, Jospin said: "We have to look for quite flexible methods, not be ideological and not refuse industrial reality in the name of non-privatisation, nor seek to privatise systematically."
"We will look for the best solutions case-by-case and we will explain them overall to the French people," he said.
He renewed his pledge to consult the personnel of France Telecom before any decision to go ahead with selling a stake in the state telecommunications company.

"I will be guided by industrial logic, for example in the defence industries...and the national interest. I will also (take into account) the cost to the state and thus to the taxpayer of frequent capital increases in a number of sectors, such as banks in difficulty," Jospin said.
"I am not sure it is the state's role to keep on bailing out financial institutions in trouble, especially since it cannot always be done under (European Union) law with the Commission," he added.
